Theme

Money, work & business · Church life

alms noun

also almsgiving, give alms, handout, charity (giving to the poor), charitable giving

classical

Sen. Vit. Beat. 25.1: quī manum ad stipem porrigunt, those who hold out their hand for alms
Suet. Aug. 91.2: stipem … ēmendīcābat ā populō
M-O s.v. charity: contribution or donation, alms

stips, stipis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a small coin given; alms

A small coin given to a beggar, or offered to a god (Lewis & Short); the nominative is not found.

Other words

  • eleēmosyna, eleēmosynae f. — alms, almsgiving (Christian Latin)

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Mt. 6.3: Tē autem faciente eleēmosynam; Tert. Patient. 7 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. charity: contribution or donation, alms; Levi–Bini p. 24 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Greek ἐλεημοσύνη, mercy: the word of the Gospels and the Church, also written elēmosyna. To give alms, eleēmosynam facere (Vulg. Mt. 6.2).

Examples

  • In Sublicium pontem mē trānsfer et inter egentēs abjice: nōn ideō tamen mē dēspiciam quod in illōrum numerō cōnsēderō quī manum ad stipem porrigunt.

    Put me on the Sublician bridge and throw me among the needy: I shall not despise myself for sitting among those who hold out their hand for alms.Sen. Vit. Beat. 25.1

  • Ex nocturnō vīsū etiam stipem quotannīs diē certō ēmendīcābat ā populō cavam manum assēs porrigentibus praebēns.

    Because of a dream he even begged alms from the people every year on a fixed day, holding out his cupped hand to those who offered him coins.Suet. Aug. 91.2

  • Tē autem faciente eleēmosynam, nesciat sinistra tua quid faciat dextera tua

    But when you give alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand is doingVulg. Mt. 6.3

See also beggar, donate, give, tip, poor.
